content: Vat Yellow 4, also known by its chemical name dibenzochrysene-7,14-dione or 3,4:8,9-dibenzopyrene-5,10-dione, is a synthetic anthraquinone vat dye with the molecular formula C24H12O2. It appears as a viscous orange liquid. This compound is primarily utilized as a dye for textiles and paper. Additionally, in combination with benzanthrone, it has been historically employed in certain older pyrotechnic formulations to produce green and yellow-colored smoke effects. According to the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), Vat Yellow 4 is classified as a Group 3 carcinogen, indicating that there is insufficient evidence to determine its carcinogenicity in humans.
